WHEN the error budget reaches 50% consumption, THE system SHALL notify the operations team for review.

WHEN the error budget is exhausted, THE system SHALL implement a deployment freeze until the next month.

THE system SHALL track error budget consumption separately for authentication and todo operations.

WHEN an incident occurs, THE system SHALL document the impact on the error budget and root cause.

### Graceful Degradation

WHEN system availability is at risk, THE system SHALL enter degraded mode to preserve core functionality.

WHEN in degraded mode, THE system SHALL prioritize read operations over write operations.

WHEN in degraded mode, THE system SHALL disable non-essential features such as edit history viewing.

WHEN degraded mode is activated, THE system SHALL display a notification to users indicating reduced functionality.

WHEN system health is restored, THE system SHALL exit degraded mode and resume normal operations.

WHEN exiting degraded mode, THE system SHALL verify all queued operations complete successfully.

THE system SHALL maintain at least 95% functionality during degraded mode for core todo operations.

sections.heading: Service Level Agreements and Recovery
sections.content:
### Availability SLAs

THE system SHALL guarantee 99.9% availability measured on a monthly basis.

WHEN availability drops below 99.9%, THE system SHALL calculate the SLA breach duration.

WHEN an SLA breach occurs, THE system SHALL generate an incident report within 24 hours.

THE system SHALL provide availability metrics accessible to users through a status dashboard.

WHEN users access the status dashboard, THE system SHALL display current availability and historical uptime.

THE system SHALL maintain separate availability targets for different user operations:
- Authentication: 99.95%
- Todo listing: 99.9%
- Todo creation and updates: 99.8%

WHEN any operation falls below its target, THE system SHALL escalate to the operations team.

### Reliability Metrics

THE system SHALL track mean time between failures (MTBF) with a target of 720 hours.

THE system SHALL track mean time to recovery (MTTR) with a target of 30 minutes.

WHEN MTTR exceeds 30 minutes, THE system SHALL trigger a post-incident review.

THE system SHALL maintain a reliability score based on MTBF and MTTR metrics.

WHEN reliability score drops below 90%, THE system SHALL initiate improvement procedures.

THE system SHALL log all reliability events with timestamps for audit purposes.

### Error Handling and Recovery

WHEN an error occurs during todo operations, THE system SHALL preserve user data before reporting the error.

WHEN a network timeout occurs, THE system SHALL retry the operation with exponential backoff.

WHEN the system detects data corruption, THE system SHALL restore from the last known good state.

THE system SHALL maintain transaction logs to enable recovery to any point within the last 24 hours.

WHEN recovery is initiated, THE system SHALL validate data integrity before resuming operations.

THE system SHALL provide users with confirmation that their data is preserved during error conditions.

WHEN an error affects multiple users, THE system SHALL prioritize recovery based on data impact.

sections.heading: Data Integrity and Storage
sections.content: Data integrity constraints and storage requirements.

sections.heading: Data Integrity and Storage
sections.content: Define backup policies, data retention, and storage tier requirements.

sections.heading: Data Integrity
sections.content:
THE system SHALL ensure that all User data remains accurate and uncorrupted throughout its lifecycle.

WHEN a User creates a Todo, THE system SHALL record the creation with a timestamp.
WHEN a User updates a Todo, THE system SHALL create a TodoHistory entry before applying changes.
WHEN a Todo is soft-deleted, THE system SHALL preserve all associated TodoHistory entries.
WHEN a Todo is permanently deleted from trash, THE system SHALL also delete all associated TodoHistory entries.

IF a write operation fails, THE system SHALL roll back all changes to maintain data consistency.
IF a read operation encounters corrupted data, THE system SHALL return an error and log the incident.

THE system SHALL prevent concurrent modifications to the same Todo from causing data loss.
THE system SHALL validate all date fields (startDate, dueDate) before persisting changes.
THE system SHALL ensure that the completed status toggle is atomic and cannot be partially applied.

WHEN the system detects data corruption, THE system SHALL notify administrators and prevent affected data from being served to users.

sections.heading: Backup Policies
sections.content:
THE system SHALL maintain regular backups of all User data, Todo records, and TodoHistory entries.

WHEN a backup is scheduled, THE system SHALL capture a consistent snapshot of all data.
WHEN a backup completes successfully, THE system SHALL verify data integrity before marking it complete.
WHEN a backup fails, THE system SHALL retry according to the backup retry policy and alert administrators.

THE system SHALL store backups in geographically redundant locations.
THE system SHALL encrypt all backup data at rest.
THE system SHALL test backup restoration procedures periodically to ensure recoverability.

IF a User requests account recovery after data loss, THE system SHALL restore data from the most recent valid backup.
IF multiple backups exist, THE system SHALL prefer the most recent backup that passes integrity verification.

THE system SHALL retain backup copies for a minimum period to support recovery scenarios.
THE system SHALL purge expired backups according to the retention policy.

sections.heading: Data Retention
sections.content:
THE system SHALL enforce data retention policies for all User and Todo data.

WHEN a User deletes their account, THE system SHALL permanently remove all associated data including Todos and TodoHistory.
WHEN a Todo is permanently deleted from trash, THE system SHALL remove all associated TodoHistory entries.

THE system SHALL retain soft-deleted Todos in trash until the User restores them or permanently deletes them.
THE system SHALL retain TodoHistory entries as long as the parent Todo exists.

IF a User requests data export, THE system SHALL provide all their data before account deletion.
IF data retention policies change, THE system SHALL apply new policies only to data created after the policy change.

THE system SHALL not retain data beyond what is necessary for the application's business purpose.
THE system SHALL securely purge data that has exceeded its retention period.

sections.heading: Storage Requirements
sections.content:
THE system SHALL store all User data, Todo records, and TodoHistory entries in a reliable storage system.

THE system SHALL ensure that all data is persisted before confirming write operations to users.
THE system SHALL use appropriate storage tiers based on data access patterns.

WHEN storing TodoHistory, THE system SHALL maintain chronological order for each Todo.
WHEN storing soft-deleted Todos, THE system SHALL mark them with a deletion timestamp.

IF storage capacity reaches a critical threshold, THE system SHALL alert administrators and prevent new writes.
IF storage performance degrades, THE system SHALL scale storage resources to maintain service levels.

THE system SHALL encrypt all data at rest in the storage system.
THE system SHALL ensure that storage operations do not expose data to unauthorized access.

sections.heading: Data Consistency
sections.content:
THE system SHALL ensure data consistency across all read and write operations.

WHEN a User updates a Todo, THE system SHALL ensure all related TodoHistory entries remain consistent.
WHEN a Todo is marked complete or incomplete, THE system SHALL update the status atomically.

IF a read operation occurs during a write, THE system SHALL return either the old or new state, not a partial state.
IF multiple users attempt to modify the same Todo simultaneously, THE system SHALL serialize the operations.

THE system SHALL ensure that soft-deleted Todos remain invisible in normal todo lists.
THE system SHALL ensure that permanently deleted Todos cannot be recovered.

WHEN restoring a Todo from trash, THE system SHALL restore all associated TodoHistory entries.
WHEN querying Todo lists with filters or sorting, THE system SHALL return consistent results for the same query parameters.

THE system SHALL validate that all date relationships (startDate before dueDate) are maintained after updates.

sections.heading: Audit and Observability
sections.content: Define audit logging, monitoring, alerting, and observability requirements.

sections.heading: Audit and Observability Requirements
sections.content:
### Audit Trail Capture

WHEN a user creates a todo, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the action type, timestamp, and todo identifier.

WHEN a user edits a todo's title, description, start date, or due date, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the changed fields and previous values.

WHEN a user marks a todo as complete or incomplete, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the completion state change.

WHEN a user deletes a todo (soft delete), THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the todo identifier and deletion timestamp.

WHEN a user restores a todo from trash, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the restoration timestamp.

WHEN a user permanently deletes a todo from trash, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the permanent deletion timestamp.

WHEN a user creates an account, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the user identifier and creation timestamp.

WHEN a user deletes their account, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the account identifier and deletion timestamp.

WHEN a user changes their password, THE system SHALL record an audit entry with the password change timestamp.

THE system SHALL ensure all audit entries are immutable once created.

THE system SHALL include the user identifier, action type, timestamp, and affected resource identifier in every audit entry.

THE system SHALL retain audit entries for a minimum period defined by data retention policy (defined in Data Retention section).

### Audit Trail Access and Integrity

WHEN an authorized user requests audit trail data, THE system SHALL return entries filtered by user, resource, or time range.

THE system SHALL prevent unauthorized users from accessing audit trail data for resources they do not own.

THE system SHALL ensure audit entries cannot be modified or deleted after creation.

THE system SHALL provide audit entry timestamps in a consistent timezone format.

### System Logging

WHEN a user authentication attempt occurs, THE system SHALL log the attempt with success or failure status.

WHEN an authorization failure occurs, THE system SHALL log the failure with the user identifier and attempted action.

WHEN a system error occurs, THE system SHALL log the error with severity level, stack trace, and context information.

WHEN a data access violation occurs, THE system SHALL log the violation with the user identifier and attempted resource.

THE system SHALL include timestamp, severity level, event type, and relevant context in every log entry.

THE system SHALL categorize log entries by severity: debug, info, warning, error, critical.

THE system SHALL ensure log entries are written atomically to prevent partial or corrupted entries.

### Monitoring Requirements

THE system SHALL monitor API response times and track percentile distributions (p50, p95, p99).

THE system SHALL monitor database query performance and track slow query thresholds.

THE system SHALL monitor error rates and track by error type and frequency.

THE system SHALL monitor user activity patterns to detect anomalies.

THE system SHALL monitor system resource utilization including CPU, memory, and storage.

THE system SHALL provide real-time visibility into system health through dashboards.

THE system SHALL maintain monitoring data for trend analysis and capacity planning.

### Alerting Policies

WHEN error rates exceed a defined threshold, THE system SHALL trigger an alert to operations personnel.

WHEN API response times exceed a defined threshold, THE system SHALL trigger an alert to operations personnel.

WHEN authentication failure rates spike beyond normal patterns, THE system SHALL trigger a security alert.

WHEN system resources approach capacity limits, THE system SHALL trigger a capacity alert.

WHEN database query performance degrades beyond acceptable thresholds, THE system SHALL trigger a performance alert.

THE system SHALL route alerts to appropriate channels based on severity and category.

THE system SHALL prevent alert fatigue by implementing alert deduplication and cooldown periods.

THE system SHALL provide alert acknowledgment and resolution tracking.

### Observability Requirements

THE system SHALL provide centralized log aggregation from all system components.

THE system SHALL support log querying and filtering by time range, severity, and event type.

THE system SHALL provide metrics dashboards for system health visualization.

THE system SHALL support distributed tracing for multi-component request flows.

THE system SHALL ensure observability data is accessible only to authorized operations personnel.

THE system SHALL maintain observability data retention consistent with security and compliance requirements.

THE system SHALL provide observability data export capabilities for external analysis tools.

sections.heading: Concurrency and Data Consistency
sections.content: Concurrency control policies, race condition handling, and data consistency guarantees.

sections.heading: Concurrency Control Policies
sections.content: Define optimistic/pessimistic locking strategies, conflict resolution, and retry semantics for concurrent operations.

sections.heading: Concurrent Update Detection
sections.content:
WHEN a user updates a todo, THE system SHALL detect if the todo has been modified by another operation since it was last read.

WHEN the system detects a concurrent modification, THE system SHALL reject the update request.

WHEN a user views a todo, THE system SHALL provide information that enables conflict detection on subsequent updates.

THE system SHALL ensure that only one update operation succeeds when multiple operations target the same todo simultaneously.

THE system SHALL prevent data loss when concurrent updates occur by rejecting conflicting operations.

THE system SHALL maintain the integrity of todo data during concurrent access scenarios.

IF a user attempts to update a todo that has been modified, THE system SHALL return the current state of the todo along with the conflict indication.

sections.heading: Optimistic Locking Strategy
sections.content:
WHEN a user submits an update to a todo, THE system SHALL verify the todo version or timestamp before applying changes.

WHEN the verification fails due to a version mismatch, THE system SHALL treat this as a conflict condition.

THE system SHALL use optimistic locking to detect conflicts without holding locks during user interaction.

WHEN a conflict is detected, THE system SHALL not apply the pending changes to the todo.

THE system SHALL track modification information for each todo to enable conflict detection.

WHEN multiple users attempt to update the same todo, THE system SHALL allow only the first valid update to succeed.

THE system SHALL reject subsequent updates that reference stale version information.

WHEN an update succeeds, THE system SHALL update the version or timestamp to reflect the new state.

sections.heading: Conflict Resolution
sections.content:
WHEN a conflict is detected during a todo update, THE system SHALL reject the update operation.

WHEN an update is rejected due to conflict, THE system SHALL return the current state of the todo to the user.

WHEN a conflict occurs, THE system SHALL provide information about what fields were changed in the conflicting update.

THE system SHALL allow the user to review the current todo state after a conflict.

THE system SHALL enable the user to retry the update operation with the latest todo data.

WHEN a user retries an update after a conflict, THE system SHALL process the retry as a new update operation.

THE system SHALL NOT automatically merge conflicting changes from different operations.

WHEN a conflict prevents an update, THE system SHALL preserve all data from both the original and conflicting updates.

sections.heading: Race Condition Prevention
sections.content:
WHEN a user performs operations on a todo while another operation is in progress, THE system SHALL prevent race conditions.

THE system SHALL ensure that todo state transitions are atomic and cannot be interrupted mid-operation.

WHEN a completion status toggle is requested, THE system SHALL process it as a single atomic operation.

WHEN a todo is deleted while another operation targets it, THE system SHALL handle the race condition appropriately.

THE system SHALL prevent duplicate history entries from being created due to concurrent edit operations.

WHEN concurrent operations target the same todo, THE system SHALL serialize them to maintain consistency.

THE system SHALL ensure that edit history reflects the actual sequence of successful updates.

IF a race condition is detected, THE system SHALL fail the operation safely without corrupting data.

sections.heading: Retry Semantics
sections.content:
WHEN an update operation fails due to a conflict, THE system SHALL allow the user to retry the operation.

WHEN a user retries a failed operation, THE system SHALL require the user to fetch the latest todo state first.

THE system SHALL NOT automatically retry failed operations without user consent.

WHEN a retry is initiated, THE system SHALL validate the new request against the current todo state.

THE system SHALL provide clear feedback when a retry is needed due to a conflict.

WHEN multiple retries fail consecutively, THE system SHALL inform the user to refresh their view of the todo.

THE system SHALL limit the number of automatic retries to prevent infinite retry loops.

WHEN a user successfully retries an operation, THE system SHALL process it with the same validation rules as the original request.

sections.heading: Data Consistency Guarantees
sections.content: Define consistency models, transactional boundary requirements, and idempotency guarantees.

sections.heading: Consistency Model
sections.content:
THE system SHALL maintain eventual consistency for all user-visible data operations.

WHEN a user performs a write operation on their todos, THE system SHALL:
1. Ensure the operation completes atomically before confirming success to the user
2. Propagate the change to all replicas within 500ms
3. Return the updated state immediately after successful commit

WHEN reading todo data, THE system SHALL:
1. Return the most recently committed version of the data
2. Ensure read-after-write consistency for the user's own data
3. Allow stale reads of up to 1 second for list operations under high load

IF a consistency conflict is detected during concurrent updates, THE system SHALL:
1. Reject the later write operation with a conflict error
2. Return the current state of the data to the client
3. Require the client to refresh and retry the operation

THE system SHALL guarantee that edit history entries are created atomically with todo updates (defined in Edit History section of 03-functional-requirements.md).

sections.heading: Transaction Boundaries
sections.content:
THE system SHALL define transaction boundaries for the following operations:

WHEN creating a todo, THE system SHALL:
1. Create the todo record and its initial state within a single transaction
2. Ensure no partial state is visible if the operation fails
3. Roll back all changes if any part of the operation fails

WHEN updating a todo, THE system SHALL:
1. Update the todo fields and create a history entry within a single transaction
2. Ensure the history entry reflects the exact state before the update
3. Roll back both the todo update and history creation if either fails

WHEN deleting a todo (soft delete), THE system SHALL:
1. Set the deletedAt timestamp and remove from active list within a single transaction
2. Ensure the todo remains accessible in trash immediately after deletion
3. Roll back if the soft delete operation fails

WHEN permanently deleting a todo from trash, THE system SHALL:
1. Delete the todo and all associated history entries within a single transaction
2. Ensure no orphaned history entries remain after deletion
3. Roll back all deletions if any part fails

WHEN restoring a todo from trash, THE system SHALL:
1. Clear the deletedAt timestamp and restore to active list within a single transaction
2. Ensure all history entries remain intact after restoration
3. Roll back if the restoration fails

WHEN deleting a user account, THE system SHALL:
1. Delete the user, all their todos, and all history entries within a single transaction
2. Ensure no orphaned todos or history entries remain after account deletion
3. Roll back the entire operation if any part fails

IF a transaction exceeds 10 seconds, THE system SHALL:
1. Automatically abort the transaction
2. Return a timeout error to the client
3. Log the timeout for monitoring purposes

sections.heading: Atomicity Guarantees
sections.content:
THE system SHALL guarantee atomicity for the following operations:

Ubiquitous: THE system SHALL ensure that all multi-step operations complete entirely or not at all.

WHEN a todo is created, THE system SHALL:
1. Atomically create the todo with default incomplete status
2. Ensure the todo is not visible until the entire operation succeeds
3. Reject the operation if any validation fails before creating the record

WHEN a todo is marked complete or incomplete, THE system SHALL:
1. Atomically toggle the completed status
2. Ensure the status change is immediately visible to the user
3. Prevent partial state where the operation is in progress

WHEN editing todo fields, THE system SHALL:
1. Atomically update all changed fields in a single operation
2. Create exactly one history entry for the complete set of changes
3. Prevent scenarios where some fields update but history is not recorded

WHEN filtering and paginating todo lists, THE system SHALL:
1. Ensure the filter criteria and pagination are applied atomically
2. Return a consistent snapshot of the data for the entire page
3. Prevent pages from showing mixed states during concurrent updates

IF an atomic operation fails mid-execution, THE system SHALL:
1. Leave the data in its pre-operation state
2. Not expose any intermediate or partial states
3. Return a clear error indicating the operation did not complete

sections.heading: Idempotency Guarantees
sections.content:
THE system SHALL provide idempotency for the following operations:

Ubiquitous: THE system SHALL ensure that repeating the same operation with identical inputs produces the same result without unintended side effects.

WHEN creating a todo with an idempotency key, THE system SHALL:
1. Return the existing todo if the same idempotency key is used again
2. Not create duplicate todo records for repeated requests
3. Return the original creation timestamp for idempotent replays

WHEN updating a todo with an idempotency key, THE system SHALL:
1. Apply the update only once even if the request is retried
2. Create only one history entry for the logical update operation
3. Return the same updated state for repeated identical requests

WHEN deleting or restoring a todo, THE system SHALL:
1. Return success if the operation was already completed
2. Not create duplicate history entries for repeated delete/restore requests
3. Maintain the correct final state regardless of retry count

WHEN a request times out without a response, THE system SHALL:
1. Allow the client to retry with the same idempotency key
2. Process the retry as the original operation if still in progress
3. Return the result of the original operation once completed

IF an operation cannot be made idempotent, THE system SHALL:
1. Return a clear error indicating the operation is not retry-safe
2. Provide guidance on how to safely retry the operation
3. Log the non-idempotent retry attempt for monitoring

THE system SHALL support idempotency keys for all write operations (create, update, delete, restore) with a minimum retention period of 24 hours.

deploymentRequirements.text: The system shall store all User data, Todo records, and TodoHistory entries in a reliable storage system.
The system shall use appropriate storage tiers based on data access patterns.
The system shall maintain regular backups of all User data, Todo records, and TodoHistory entries.
The system shall store backups in geographically redundant locations.
The system shall encrypt all backup data at rest.

authRequirements.text: When a user registers for an account, the system shall require a password that meets minimum security complexity requirements.
When a user logs in, the system shall authenticate using their email and password credentials.
When a user changes their password, the system shall require verification of the current password before accepting the new password.
When a user's password is stored, the system shall hash it using a secure password hashing algorithm.
When a user logs in successfully, the system shall create an authenticated session.
When a session expires, the system shall require the user to re-authenticate.
When a user logs out, the system shall invalidate their session.
When multiple failed login attempts occur, the system shall implement account lockout or cooldown mechanisms to prevent brute force attacks.
When a user accesses the system, the system shall ensure they can only view and modify their own todos.
When a user requests todo data, the system shall verify the user owns the requested todos before returning any data.
When a user creates a todo, the system shall associate it exclusively with the authenticated user.
When a user deletes their account, the system shall permanently remove all their todos and associated history.
If a user attempts to access another user's todo, the system shall reject the request without revealing whether the todo exists.
If a user attempts to perform an action on a todo they do not own, the system shall reject the request with a generic permission error.
The system shall ensure complete data isolation between users at all levels of the application.
When a guest makes API requests, the system shall limit requests to 100 per hour per IP address.
When a member makes API requests, the system shall limit requests to 1000 per hour per user account.
When a user exceeds the rate limit, the system shall return a 429 Too Many Requests response.
When the rate limit is exceeded, the system shall include a Retry-After header indicating when the user can retry.
When a user attempts more than 10 failed login attempts within 5 minutes, the system shall require CAPTCHA verification.
When suspicious bulk operations are detected, the system shall flag the account for review.
When abuse is confirmed, the system shall suspend the offending account pending manual review.
When a user is flagged for abuse, the system shall notify them of the restriction and appeal process.

dataProtection.text: When user credentials are transmitted over the network, the system shall encrypt them using TLS/SSL encryption.
When password data is stored, the system shall encrypt it at rest using secure encryption standards.
When sensitive user data is transmitted, the system shall use encrypted communication channels.
When session tokens are generated, the system shall ensure they are cryptographically secure and random.
When session tokens are transmitted, the system shall mark them as secure and http-only to prevent client-side script access.
If encryption keys are compromised, the system shall have a procedure to rotate keys and re-encrypt affected data.
If data is stored in backups, the system shall ensure backups are also encrypted.
When a user submits input data, the system shall validate all input before processing.
When a user enters a display name, the system shall validate it does not exceed the maximum allowed length.
When a user enters a todo title, the system shall validate it is not empty and does not exceed the maximum allowed length.
When a user enters a todo description, the system shall validate it does not exceed the maximum allowed length.
When a user enters dates, the system shall validate the date format is correct and the dates are logically valid.
When a user submits any form data, the system shall sanitize input to prevent injection attacks.
When a user submits HTML or special characters, the system shall escape or sanitize them to prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.
If input validation fails, the system shall reject the request and return a generic error message without exposing internal details.
If input contains potentially malicious content, the system shall log the attempt for security monitoring.
The system shall follow OWASP Top 10 security guidelines to protect against common web vulnerabilities.
The system shall implement protection against SQL injection attacks through parameterized queries and input validation.
The system shall implement protection against cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks through output encoding and content security policies.
The system shall implement protection against cross-site request forgery (CSRF) through token validation on state-changing operations.
The system shall implement protection against broken authentication through secure session management and password policies.
The system shall implement protection against sensitive data exposure through encryption and access controls.
The system shall implement protection against security misconfiguration through regular security audits and secure default configurations.
The system shall implement protection against insufficient logging and monitoring through comprehensive security event logging.
The system shall ensure that all User data remains accurate and uncorrupted throughout its lifecycle.
When a Todo is soft-deleted, the system shall preserve all associated TodoHistory entries.
When a Todo is permanently deleted from trash, the system shall also delete all associated TodoHistory entries.
If a write operation fails, the system shall roll back all changes to maintain data consistency.
If a read operation encounters corrupted data, the system shall return an error and log the incident.
The system shall prevent concurrent modifications to the same Todo from causing data loss.
The system shall validate all date fields (startDate, dueDate) before persisting changes.
The system shall ensure that the completed status toggle is atomic and cannot be partially applied.
When the system detects data corruption, the system shall notify administrators and prevent affected data from being served to users.
The system shall encrypt all data at rest in the storage system.
The system shall ensure that storage operations do not expose data to unauthorized access.

text: I'll now design the database schema based on your multi-user Todo application requirements. The analyze phase has been completed successfully, so we can proceed with the database design.

instruction:
Multi-User Todo Application Database Requirements:

## User Account
- Users sign up with email and password
- Users log in with email and password
- Users can change their password
- Users can delete their account (all their todos, including those in trash, are permanently deleted)

## User Profile
- Each user has a profile with: display name
- Users can edit their display name
- Users cannot view other users' profiles (this is a private todo app)

## Creating Todos
- Users can create a todo with:
  - Title (required)
  - Description (optional, can be left empty)
  - Start date (optional, can be left empty)
  - Due date (optional, can be left empty)
- Newly created todos are incomplete by default

## Viewing Todos
- Users can view a list of their own todos
- The list is paginated
- Each todo in the list shows: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date
- Users can view a single todo to see all its details including full description

## Completing Todos
- Users can mark a todo as complete
- Users can mark a todo as incomplete
- This is a simple toggle between two states

## Editing Todos
- Users can edit their todo's title, description, start date, and due date
- Every edit is recorded in the todo's history

## Edit History
- Each todo has an edit history
- Every time a todo is edited, a history entry is created
- Each history entry records:
  - When the edit was made
  - What the title was changed to (if changed)
  - What the description was changed to (if changed)
  - What the start date was changed to (if changed)
  - What the due date was changed to (if changed)
- Users can view the full edit history of any of their todos
- History entries are sorted from most recent to oldest

## Deleting Todos
- Users can delete their own todos
- Deleted todos are not permanently removed (soft delete)
- Deleted todos no longer appear in the normal todo list

## Trash
- Users can view a list of their deleted todos (trash)
- The trash list is paginated
- Users can restore a deleted todo from the trash (it returns to the normal todo list)
- Users can permanently delete a todo from the trash
- Permanently deleting a todo also deletes its edit history

## Filtering Todos
- Users can filter their todo list by completion status:
  - All todos
  - Only complete todos
  - Only incomplete todos

## Sorting Todos
- Users can sort their todo list by:
  - Creation date (newest first or oldest first)
  - Start date (earliest first or latest first)
  - Due date (earliest first or latest first)
- Todos without a start date appear at the end when sorting by start date
- Todos without a due date appear at the end when sorting by due date

## Privacy
- Each user's todos are completely private
- Users can only see their own todos
- There is no way to view, access, or share another user's todos

models.name: todo_app_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for anonymous browsing identified by device fingerprint.

Guest actors represent unauthenticated users who can access the system without email/password registration. Each guest is uniquely identified by their device fingerprint, enabling session persistence across requests from the same device.

Key characteristics:
- No email/password authentication (use todo_app_members for registered users)
- Device fingerprint serves as unique identifier
- Supports temporary session management via todo_app_guest_sessions
- Soft delete support for guest account cleanup

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest device. Used for guest identification and session association.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Null if the account is active.

models.name: todo_app_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access with short expiration. Tracks connection metadata for unauthenticated guest users including IP address, URL, and referrer information for session auditing and security purposes.

This session table belongs to the {@link todo_app_guests} actor table and stores append-only login session records. Each guest can have multiple concurrent sessions, and sessions are automatically expired based on the expired_at timestamp for security.

Key characteristics:
- Append-only audit trail of guest login events
- Managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD
- Short expiration period for temporary guest access
- Connection context for security monitoring

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Client URL for session tracking and context.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Client referrer URL for session tracking and context.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp for audit trail.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp for security enforcement.

models.name: todo_app_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email/password authentication credentials and profile data.

This table represents the canonical identity records for authenticated members in the system. Each member owns their private todo items and has one-to-many sessions stored in the {@link todo_app_member_sessions} table.

Key relationships:
- Owns {@link todo_app_todos} via userId foreign key
- Has {@link todo_app_member_sessions} for authentication
- Has {@link todo_app_member_password_resets} for password recovery
- Has {@link todo_app_member_email_verifications} for registration confirmation

Account deletion triggers cascade deletion of all owned todos and their histories.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address for authentication. Must be unique across all members.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: User's display name (1-100 characters). Visible in the user's profile.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Account creation timestamp. Immutable after registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp. Updated on profile changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for account deletion. When set, account is considered deleted and all owned data is permanently removed.

models.name: todo_app_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with connection metadata and temporal tracking. Each session record captures a single login event for a {@link todo_app_members} member, storing IP address, request context, and expiration information for security auditing and session management.

Sessions are append-only audit trail entries that track when members authenticate to the system. Each member can have multiple active sessions simultaneously, enabling multi-device access while maintaining security through expiration policies.

Related to {@link todo_app_members} through a 1:N relationship where one member owns many sessions.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who owns this session. {@link todo_app_members.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client that created this session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the login endpoint or page where authentication occurred.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer header from the client request during login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created (login time).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid for authentication.

models.name: todo_app_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for account recovery workflow.

Stores one-time use tokens generated when members request password resets. Each token is associated with a specific member and has an expiration time after which it becomes invalid. Tokens are consumed upon successful password reset and cannot be reused.

This table supports the password change workflow by providing secure, time-limited tokens that verify the member's identity before allowing password modification. Tokens are automatically cleaned up after expiration or consumption.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token. Generated cryptographically secure random string for one-time use.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Token becomes invalid after this time and cannot be used for password reset.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp. When the password reset token was generated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp. Updated when token is consumed or modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when token is consumed or manually invalidated.

models.name: todo_app_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for new member registration confirmation. Each verification record stores a unique token sent to the member's email address, with expiration timestamp for security. Used in the registration workflow to confirm email ownership before activating the account.

This table supports the member registration process by:
- Storing verification tokens with expiration
- Linking to the pending member account via {@link todo_app_members.id}
- Enabling token validation during email confirmation
- Supporting token renewal through new verification records

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member account awaiting email verification. {@link todo_app_members.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Cryptographically secure verification token sent to the member's email address.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Tokens are invalid after this time.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the email was successfully verified. Null if not yet verified.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for cleanup.

models.name: todo_app_todo_histories
models.description: Edit history entries for todos, recording timestamp and changed field values. Each entry is created when a todo is edited, storing the new values of title, description, startDate, dueDate, and completed status that were modified. This table serves as an append-only audit trail that users can view to track the complete modification history of their todos, sorted from most recent to oldest. History entries are automatically deleted when the parent todo is permanently removed from the trash.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the edit was made and history entry was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the history entry was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the history entry was soft-deleted.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title value at the time of edit. Null if title was not changed in this edit.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description value at the time of edit. Null if description was not changed in this edit.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Start date value at the time of edit. Null if start date was not changed or not set in this edit.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Due date value at the time of edit. Null if due date was not changed or not set in this edit.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status at the time of edit. Null if completion status was not changed in this edit.

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Core todo items with title, description, dates, completion status, and soft delete. Owned by members via todo_app_member_id foreign key for data isolation and privacy enforcement.

Each todo represents a task that can be created, edited, completed, and deleted by its owner. Soft deletion enables trash management where deleted todos can be restored or permanently removed.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link todo_app_members} for ownership
- Has many {@link todo_app_todo_histories} for edit audit trail (managed separately)

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description: Owner member's {@link todo_app_members.id}. Enforces data isolation and privacy - members can only access their own todos.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Todo title (required, 1-500 characters). The main descriptive text for the task.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Todo description (optional, 0-2000 characters). Additional details about the task.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Optional start date for the todo. Used for sorting and filtering tasks by when they begin.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date for the todo. Used for sorting and filtering tasks by deadline.

plainFields.name: completed
plainFields.description: Completion status. True when the todo is marked as complete, false otherwise. Defaults to false when created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was created. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was last updated. Automatically updated on any modification.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted. Null for active todos, set to current time when deleted. Enables trash management and restoration.

### `todo_app_guests`

Temporary guest accounts for anonymous browsing identified by device
fingerprint.

Guest actors represent unauthenticated users who can access the system
without email/password registration. Each guest is uniquely identified by
their device fingerprint, enabling session persistence across requests
from the same device.

Key characteristics:
- No email/password authentication (use todo_app_members for registered
users)
- Device fingerprint serves as unique identifier
- Supports temporary session management via todo_app_guest_sessions
- Soft delete support for guest account cleanup

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `device_fingerprint`
  > Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest device. Used for guest
  > identification and session association.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted. Null if the account is
  > active.

### `todo_app_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access with short expiration. Tracks
connection metadata for unauthenticated guest users including IP address,
URL, and referrer information for session auditing and security purposes.

This session table belongs to the [todo_app_guests](#todo_app_guests) actor table and
stores append-only login session records. Each guest can have multiple
concurrent sessions, and sessions are automatically expired based on the
expired_at timestamp for security.

Key characteristics:
- Append-only audit trail of guest login events
- Managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD
- Short expiration period for temporary guest access
- Connection context for security monitoring

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_guest_id`: Belonged guest's [todo_app_guests.id](#todo_app_guests).
- `ip`: Client IP address for session tracking and security auditing.
- `href`: Client URL for session tracking and context.
- `referrer`: Client referrer URL for session tracking and context.
- `created_at`: Session creation timestamp for audit trail.
- `expired_at`: Session expiration timestamp for security enforcement.

### `todo_app_members`

Registered member accounts with email/password authentication credentials
and profile data.

This table represents the canonical identity records for authenticated
members in the system. Each member owns their private todo items and has
one-to-many sessions stored in the [todo_app_member_sessions](#todo_app_member_sessions)
table.

Key relationships:
- Owns [todo_app_todos](#todo_app_todos) via userId foreign key
- Has [todo_app_member_sessions](#todo_app_member_sessions) for authentication
- Has [todo_app_member_password_resets](#todo_app_member_password_resets) for password recovery
- Has [todo_app_member_email_verifications](#todo_app_member_email_verifications) for registration

histories.

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`

- `password_hash`: Hashed password for secure authentication. Never stored in plain text.
- `display_name`: User's display name (1-100 characters). Visible in the user's profile.
- `created_at`: Account creation timestamp. Immutable after registration.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp. Updated on profile changes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp for account deletion. When set, account is

### `todo_app_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens for member authentication with connection metadata and

a [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) member, storing IP address, request context,
and expiration information for security auditing and session management.

Sessions are append-only audit trail entries that track when members
authenticate to the system. Each member can have multiple active sessions

through expiration policies.

Related to [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) through a 1:N relationship where one
member owns many sessions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`: Member who owns this session. [todo_app_members.id](#todo_app_members).
- `ip`: IP address of the client that created this session.
- `href`: URL of the login endpoint or page where authentication occurred.
- `referrer`: Referrer header from the client request during login.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this session was created (login time).
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid for

### `todo_app_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with expiration for account recovery workflow.

Stores one-time use tokens generated when members request password
resets. Each token is associated with a specific member and has an
expiration time after which it becomes invalid. Tokens are consumed upon
successful password reset and cannot be reused.

This table supports the password change workflow by providing secure,
time-limited tokens that verify the member's identity before allowing
password modification. Tokens are automatically cleaned up after
expiration or consumption.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `todo_app_member_id`: Member requesting password reset. [todo_app_members.id](#todo_app_members).
- `token`

Edit history entries for todos, recording timestamp and changed field

- `due_date`

### `todo_app_todos`

Core todo items with title, description, dates, completion status, and
soft delete. Owned by members via todo_app_member_id foreign key for data
isolation and privacy enforcement.

Each todo represents a task that can be created, edited, completed, and
deleted by its owner. Soft deletion enables trash management where
deleted todos can be restored or permanently removed.

Relationships:
- Belongs to [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) for ownership
- Has many [todo_app_todo_histories](#todo_app_todo_histories) for edit audit trail (managed

- `description`
  > Todo description (optional, 0-2000 characters). Additional details about

- `start_date`
  > Optional start date for the todo. Used for sorting and filtering tasks by
  > when they begin.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date for the todo. Used for sorting and filtering tasks by

- `completed`
  > Completion status. True when the todo is marked as complete, false
  > otherwise. Defaults to false when created.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the todo was created. Immutable after creation.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was last updated. Automatically updated on any
  > modification.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted. Null for active todos, set to
  > current time when deleted. Enables trash management and restoration.

instruction:
Multi-User Todo Application API Requirements:

## User Account Endpoints
- Sign up with email and password
- Log in with email and password
- Change password (authenticated user)
- Delete account (authenticated user, permanently deletes all todos including trash)

## User Profile Endpoints
- View own profile (display name)
- Edit own profile (display name)
- Cannot view other users' profiles

## Todo Endpoints
- Create todo with: title (required), description (optional), start date (optional), due date (optional)
- List todos (paginated) with filters and sorting
  - Filter by completion status: all, complete, incomplete
  - Sort by: creation date (newest/oldest), start date (earliest/latest), due date (earliest/latest)
  - Todos without start/due dates appear at end when sorting by those fields
- View single todo details (including full description)
- Update todo: title, description, start date, due date (every edit creates history entry)
- Toggle completion status (complete/incomplete)
- Delete todo (soft delete, moves to trash)

## Trash Endpoints
- List deleted todos (paginated)
- Restore todo from trash (returns to normal list)
- Permanently delete todo from trash (also deletes edit history)

## Edit History Endpoints
- View edit history for a todo (sorted most recent to oldest)
- Each history entry includes: timestamp, title change, description change, start date change, due date change

## Privacy Requirements
- All endpoints must enforce user isolation
- Users can only access their own todos and profile
- No sharing or cross-user access possible

operations.specification: Create new guest account with device fingerprint. 1) Validate device_fingerprint is provided and not empty. 2) Check if device_fingerprint already exists (return 409 Conflict if exists). 3) Create todo_app_guests record with device_fingerprint, set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp, deleted_at to null. 4) Create initial todo_app_guest_sessions record with the guest id, client IP from request, href and referrer from request headers. 5) Generate JWT access token and refresh token with guest actor claims. 6) Return authorized response with tokens and guest id.
operations.description:
Register a new guest user account identified by device fingerprint for anonymous access to the todo application.

This endpoint creates a temporary guest account that allows unauthenticated users to access the system without email/password registration. The guest is uniquely identified by their device fingerprint, which serves as the primary identifier for session persistence and data ownership.

The operation validates that the device fingerprint is unique - if a guest with the same fingerprint already exists, a 409 Conflict error is returned. This prevents duplicate guest accounts from the same device.

Upon successful registration, the system creates both a guest account record and an initial session record. The session tracks connection metadata including IP address, current URL, and referrer for security auditing purposes. JWT tokens are generated and returned for subsequent authenticated requests.

Guest accounts support soft deletion via the deleted_at timestamp, allowing for account cleanup while maintaining audit trails. The session records are append-only and expire based on the expired_at timestamp for security.

Related operations include refresh (POST /auth/guest/refresh) for renewing expired tokens. No login operation exists for guests as they authenticate via device fingerprint through the join flow.

requestBody.description: Guest registration information containing device fingerprint for unique identification

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing JWT tokens and guest account information

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Refresh expired JWT tokens for guest session. 1) Validate refresh token is provided and well-formed. 2) Decode and verify refresh token signature and expiration. 3) Extract guest id from token claims. 4) Verify guest account exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). 5) Find valid session record matching guest id and check if session is not expired (expired_at > now). 6) If valid, generate new access token and refresh token. 7) Update session expired_at timestamp to extend session validity. 8) Return new authorized response with refreshed tokens.
operations.description:
Renew expired JWT access and refresh tokens for an authenticated guest user session.

This endpoint allows guest users to maintain their session without re-registration by exchanging a valid refresh token for new access and refresh tokens. The refresh token is included in the request body and must be a previously issued token from the join or refresh operation.

The operation validates the refresh token's signature, expiration, and the associated guest account status. If the guest account has been soft deleted or the session has expired, a 401 Unauthorized error is returned. The session's expired_at timestamp is extended upon successful refresh to maintain session continuity.

Token refresh is essential for maintaining guest access across multiple requests without requiring the user to re-identify themselves. The JWT tokens contain the guest actor type and guest id claims for authorization on subsequent API calls.

This operation complements the join endpoint - after initial registration via join, users call refresh periodically to maintain their session. No login operation exists for guests since they authenticate through the device fingerprint join flow rather than credential-based authentication.

Related operations include join (POST /auth/guest/join) for initial guest registration and all authenticated todo operations that require valid JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for renewing expired JWT access and refresh tokens

responseBody.description: Authorized response containing new JWT tokens and guest account information

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: 1. Validate request body: email format (RFC 5322), password minimum 8 characters, display_name 1-100 characters. 2. Check email uniqueness in todo_app_members table. 3. Hash password using bcrypt with cost factor 12. 4. Create new todo_app_members record with email, password_hash, display_name, createdAt=now. 5. Generate email verification token and store in todo_app_member_email_verifications with expires_at=now+24h. 6. Send verification email to user. 7. Return IAuthorized response with temporary token (valid until email verification).
operations.description:
Register a new member account with email and password credentials. This endpoint creates a new authenticated user in the system, storing their email address, hashed password, and display name in the todo_app_members table.

The registration process performs several validation steps: email format validation following RFC 5322 standards, uniqueness check against existing members to prevent duplicate accounts, password strength validation requiring minimum 8 characters, and display name length validation (1-100 characters). Upon successful validation, the password is hashed using bcrypt with cost factor 12 before storage.

After account creation, an email verification workflow is initiated. A cryptographically secure token is generated and stored in the todo_app_member_email_verifications table with a 24-hour expiration. This verification token is sent to the provided email address, and the account remains in a pending state until the user confirms ownership by clicking the verification link.

The response includes an IAuthorized object containing temporary access credentials. These temporary tokens have limited validity and restricted permissions until email verification is completed. This security measure prevents abuse of the registration system while allowing users to begin the verification process immediately.

Related operations: After registration, users must complete email verification before accessing protected resources. The login operation (/auth/member/login) becomes available once the account is verified. Password reset functionality (/auth/member/password/reset) is available for verified accounts using the todo_app_member_password_resets table.

requestBody.description: New member registration information including email, password, and display name.

responseBody.description: Authentication response containing access tokens and member information for the newly registered account.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: 1. Validate request body: email format, password non-empty. 2. Query todo_app_members by email (case-insensitive). 3. If no record or deleted_at is set, return 401 unauthorized. 4. Verify password using bcrypt.compare() against stored password_hash. 5. If password mismatch, return 401 unauthorized. 6. Create new session record in todo_app_member_sessions with ip, href, referrer from request context, created_at=now, expired_at=now+30days. 7. Generate JWT access token and refresh token. 8. Return IAuthorized response with tokens and member profile.
operations.description:
Authenticate a registered member using email and password credentials. This endpoint validates the provided credentials against the todo_app_members table and establishes a new authenticated session.

The login process begins with credential validation: email format verification and password non-empty check. The system queries the todo_app_members table using the provided email address with case-insensitive matching. If no matching record exists, or if the account has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), the request is rejected with a 401 unauthorized response.

For valid accounts, the system performs password verification using bcrypt.compare() against the stored password_hash. This cryptographic comparison ensures secure credential validation without exposing the actual password. Failed password matching results in a 401 unauthorized response.

Upon successful authentication, a new session record is created in the todo_app_member_sessions table. This session tracks the login event with metadata including the client IP address, login page URL (href), and referrer header. The session is assigned a 30-day expiration period (expired_at) and is linked to the authenticated member via foreign key.

The response includes an IAuthorized object containing JWT access and refresh tokens. The access token is used for authenticating subsequent API requests, while the refresh token enables token renewal without requiring re-authentication. The response also includes the member's profile information (id, email, displayName) for immediate client-side use.

Update the authenticated member's profile information, specifically their display name.

This operation allows a logged-in member to modify their display name, which is a personal profile attribute stored in the `display_name` column of the `todo_app_members` table. The display name must be between 1 and 100 characters and cannot be empty or whitespace-only. Profile changes are immediately persisted and reflected in the `updated_at` timestamp.

**Security and Privacy**

The system enforces strict privacy boundaries by only allowing users to update their own profile. Cross-user profile modification is completely prohibited. The authenticated user's identity is derived from their session token, ensuring that only the account owner can make changes to their profile. The system verifies the user exists and is not soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL) before processing any updates.

**Validation Rules**

The display_name field is validated to ensure it meets length requirements (1-100 characters). Empty or whitespace-only display names are rejected with a 400 Bad Request response. The system immediately persists profile changes upon successful validation and updates the `updated_at` column to reflect the modification timestamp.

- `GET /profile` - Retrieve the current profile information
- `PUT /password` - Change the authentication password
- `DELETE /account` - Permanently delete the account and all owned data

Retrieve detailed information about a specific authentication session owned by the authenticated member.

This endpoint provides complete session metadata including the client IP address, login URL (href), referrer information, creation timestamp, and expiration timestamp. Session records serve as an audit trail for member authentication events and are used for security monitoring and session management purposes.

**Authorization**: Only the member who owns this session can access it. Members cannot view sessions belonging to other users. This enforces strict data isolation and privacy boundaries.

**Session Context**: Each session represents a single login event for a member account. Members can have multiple concurrent sessions active simultaneously, enabling multi-device access. Sessions are tracked with connection metadata for security auditing.

**Related Operations**:
- `PATCH /sessions` - List all sessions belonging to the authenticated member with pagination and filtering
- `DELETE /sessions/{sessionId}` - Revoke a specific session (logout from a specific device)

operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_sessions table by session ID (UUID primary key).

**Authorization Flow**:
1. Extract authenticated member ID from JWT token in Authorization header
2. Query todo_app_member_sessions WHERE id = sessionId AND todo_app_member_id = authenticated_member_id
3. If no matching session found, return 404 Not Found
4. If session exists but belongs to different member, return 403 Forbidden

**Database Query**:
```sql
SELECT id, todo_app_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at
FROM todo_app_member_sessions
WHERE id = $1 AND todo_app_member_id = $2
```

**Response Construction**:
- Map database row to ITodoAppMemberSession DTO
- Include all session fields: id, memberId, ip, href, referrer, createdAt, expiredAt
- Return 200 OK with session details

**Error Handling**:
- 401 Unauthorized: No valid authentication token provided
- 403 Forbidden: Session exists but belongs to different member
- 404 Not Found: Session ID not found or already deleted

**Performance Considerations**:
- Use indexed lookup on id primary key
- Filter by todo_app_member_id for data isolation
- Single row retrieval, O(1) complexity

Retrieve a specific email verification record for the authenticated member.

This endpoint allows members to check the status of their email verification, including whether the email has been verified (verified_at is set), when the verification token expires, and when the verification record was created. The verification record is stored in the todo_app_member_email_verifications table and contains a cryptographically secure token that was sent to the member's email address during the registration workflow.

**Security Considerations**

Only the member who owns the verification record can access it. The system verifies that the authenticated member's ID matches the todo_app_member_id field of the verification record before returning any data. This ownership verification prevents members from accessing verification information belonging to other users and protects against information leakage about other members' registration status.

**Soft Delete Behavior**

If the verification record has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), the endpoint returns a 404 Not Found response. Soft-deleted records are treated as non-existent to prevent access to expired or invalidated verification tokens.

**Response Data**

The response includes the verification record's ID, the expiration timestamp (expires_at), the verification completion timestamp (verified_at), and the creation timestamp (created_at). The token value itself is not exposed in the response to maintain security and prevent token replay attacks.

operations.description:
Request a password reset for a member account. This operation initiates the account recovery workflow by generating a secure, time-limited password reset token and sending reset instructions to the member's registered email address.

The password reset process is designed for members who have forgotten their password or need to reset it for security reasons. Unlike the password change operation which requires current password verification, this endpoint allows account recovery without prior authentication.

When a password reset is requested, the system generates a cryptographically secure random token that is valid for a limited time period (typically 1 hour). The token is stored in the password reset tokens table and associated with the member's account. An email containing the reset link and token is sent to the member's registered email address.

For security purposes, if the provided email address does not match any active member account, the system returns a generic success response to prevent email enumeration attacks. This ensures that attackers cannot determine which email addresses are registered in the system.

Any existing active password reset tokens for the member are automatically invalidated when a new reset is requested, ensuring only the most recent token can be used. Each token is single-use and becomes invalid immediately after successful password reset or upon expiration.

Related Operations:
- PATCH /password-resets/{token}: Execute the password reset using the token received via email
- PUT /members/{memberId}/password: Change password when current password is known (requires authentication)

operations.description:
Verify a password reset token's validity before allowing password change.

This endpoint validates whether a password reset token exists in the `todo_app_member_password_resets` table, has not expired, and has not been consumed. It is typically called before presenting the password change form to ensure the reset link is still valid.

The password reset token is stored in the `todo_app_member_password_resets` table, which contains one-time use tokens generated when members request account recovery through email. Each token is cryptographically secure, single-use, and has a limited expiration window (`expires_at`) for security purposes. Tokens are associated with a specific member via `todo_app_member_id` and are consumed upon successful password reset.

**Security Considerations**:

- Token validity is checked against the `expires_at` timestamp
- Consumed (soft-deleted with `deleted_at` set) tokens are rejected with 404
- Token details are not exposed in the response to prevent token leakage
- Only token status and expiration information is returned
- The actual `token` value is never exposed in the API response

**Related Operations**:

- Password reset request generates a new token record in `todo_app_member_password_resets` (POST /password-resets)
- Password change consumes the token by soft-deleting it upon successful verification (PUT /password-resets/{resetId})
- Tokens are automatically invalidated after expiration or consumption

**Expected Behavior**:

- Returns token validity status and expiration time for valid tokens
- Returns 404 for non-existent or already-consumed (soft-deleted) tokens
- Returns 410 for expired tokens (expires_at is in the past)
- Does not expose the actual token value in the response

Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of todo items from the `todo_app_todos` table owned by the authenticated member.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for todo management, allowing members to filter by completion status, sort by various date fields, and paginate through large result sets. The endpoint enforces strict data isolation through the `todo_app_member_id` foreign key - each member can only access their own todo items, ensuring complete privacy and security as defined in the ownership and isolation rules.

The response includes todo summaries optimized for list displays, containing essential fields like title, completion status, and key dates. Full todo details including descriptions can be retrieved via the single todo endpoint (GET /todos/{todoId}).

Filtering supports three completion status modes: 'all' returns todos regardless of completion state, 'complete' returns only completed todos, and 'incomplete' returns only pending todos. Sorting can be applied to creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order. Todos without start or due dates appear at the end when sorting by those fields, as specified in the list query specifications.

Pagination uses cursor-based navigation for efficient handling of large todo lists. The response includes pagination metadata with cursors for navigating to previous and next pages. Only active todos (where `deleted_at` IS NULL) are returned, excluding items in trash.

Related operations:
- POST /todos: Create a new todo item in the todo_app_todos table
- GET /todos/{todoId}: Retrieve detailed information for a specific todo
- PUT /todos/{todoId}: Update an existing todo item
- DELETE /todos/{todoId}: Soft delete a todo by setting deleted_at timestamp (moves to trash)
- PATCH /todos/trash: List deleted todos (where deleted_at IS NOT NULL) in trash
- POST /todos/{todoId}/restore: Restore a todo from trash by clearing deleted_at

Use cursor-based pagination with created_at or requested sort field as cursor column. Join not required for summary response. Validate sort field against allowed values (createdAt, startDate, dueDate). Validate sort direction (asc/desc). Validate page size limits (max 100). operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated member.

This endpoint allows members to create personal todo items with a required title and optional description, start date, and due date. Each todo is automatically assigned to the authenticated user via the todo_app_member_id foreign key and remains completely private to that user, enforcing data isolation as defined in the todo_app_todos table schema.

The created todo will have its completion status initialized to false. System-managed fields including the unique identifier (id), creation timestamp (created_at), and update timestamp (updated_at) are automatically populated by the server. The soft delete field (deleted_at) remains null for active todos.

**Validation Rules**:

- Title is required and must be between 1 and 500 characters (per todo_app_todos.title column constraint)
- Description is optional and can be up to 2000 characters (per todo_app_todos.description column constraint)
- Start date and due date are optional datetime fields; if both are provided, start date must be before or equal to due date
- All datetime values must be valid ISO 8601 formatted timestamps

**Security Considerations**:

- Only authenticated members can create todos (authorizationActor: member)
- The todo ownership is automatically assigned based on the authenticated session, preventing users from creating todos for other members
- Cross-user access is prevented at all levels; users can only access their own todos via the todo_app_member_id foreign key constraint

**Related Operations**:

- `PATCH /todoApp/member/todos` - List and search existing todos with filtering and pagination
- `GET /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}` - Retrieve details of a specific todo
- `PUT /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}` - Update an existing todo (automatically creates history entry in todo_app_todo_histories)
- `DELETE /todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}` - Soft delete a todo (sets deleted_at timestamp, moves to trash)

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo item by its unique identifier.

This endpoint provides detailed access to a specific todo's complete information, including its title, description, start date, due date, and current completion status. The operation returns the full todo entity with all available fields from the todo_app_todos table.

**Ownership Verification**: The system strictly enforces data isolation by verifying that the requested todo belongs to the authenticated member. Access to todos owned by other users is completely prohibited, and the system will not reveal whether a todo exists when the requesting user does not own it. This implements the data privacy and ownership rules defined in the todo_app_todos schema where todo_app_member_id enforces member ownership.

**Soft Delete Filtering**: This endpoint only returns active todos where deleted_at is NULL. Todos with a deleted_at timestamp set are excluded from results and must be accessed through trash management endpoints. The soft delete mechanism is implemented via the deleted_at column in the todo_app_todos table, allowing todos to be restored or permanently removed from trash.

**Security Considerations**: This operation requires member authentication. Guest users cannot access any todo data. The system treats unauthorized access attempts as security violations and denies them without revealing information about the existence of other users' data.

**Related Operations**: For listing todos with pagination and filtering, use `PATCH /todos`. For viewing soft-deleted todos in trash, use `PATCH /todos/trash`. For viewing edit history of this todo, use `GET /todos/{todoId}/history`.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo item with new field values for title, description, start date, and due date. This operation allows authenticated members to modify their own todos while maintaining data integrity and audit trail.

The system enforces strict data isolation to ensure members can only update their own todos by verifying the todo_app_member_id foreign key against the authenticated user's ID. When a member attempts to update a todo that belongs to another user, the request is rejected with a 403 Forbidden response. Soft deleted todos (where deleted_at is not null) in the trash cannot be updated through this endpoint and will return 404 Not Found.

Optimistic locking is implemented to prevent lost updates from concurrent modifications. The operation compares the current updated_at timestamp with the expected timestamp provided by the client. If a conflict is detected, the update is rejected with a 409 Conflict response, returning the current todo state and details about the conflicting changes. This ensures data integrity when multiple operations target the same todo simultaneously.

Every successful update automatically creates an entry in the todo_app_todo_histories table to maintain a complete audit trail. The history entry records the created_at timestamp and only the fields that were actually modified in this edit (unchanged fields are stored as null). This enables users to review the complete edit history via GET /todos/{todoId}/history and track exactly how their todos have evolved over time.

Related operations include GET /todos/{todoId} for retrieving todo details, PATCH /todos for listing todos with filtering and pagination, POST /todos for creating new todos, and GET /todos/{todoId}/history for viewing the edit history of a specific todo.
